attempts.entry_title: Morpho-electric specializations of macaque L5 ET neurons (Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. 2024)
attempts.description: Tests the physiology findings of Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. (2024) on dandiset 001065, which holds the current clamp recordings of 294 deep-layer neurons of macaque motor and temporal cortex. Features are computed from the traces; area, preparation and subclass labels come from the paper's per-cell tables on Zenodo. It compares L5 ET with other neurons, L5 ET neurons of the two areas, firing to 4 nA, irregular firing and subthreshold oscillations, and tests the dendritic findings on the paper's deposited morphology features.

outcomes.statement: The dandiset's files are the cells of the paper's per-cell tables, which supply the area, preparation and subclass labels, and the features computed here from the recordings agree with the values in those tables.
outcomes.source: The paper's code, Zenodo record 13749343 (L5_physiology_121223.csv, lockdown_physiology_072623.csv, MCx.pkl, TCx.pkl)
outcomes.notes: All 294 files match a row of L5_physiology_121223.csv by cell name; 47 of its 341 rows are not in the dataset. Donor agrees for 293 of 294 cells and species for 292 of 294 (99.3%). The median Spearman correlation over the 39 features computed here against the table's values is 0.957, with 28 of 39 features at 0.9 or more; the lowest are i_max_gain (0.33), initial_ifreq_gain (0.47) and initial_gain (0.63), and SFA correlates at -0.989 as the table holds the inverse ratio. After the sweep check, maximum and steady-state input resistance agree with the table at Pearson r 0.993 and 0.990. All 68 cells of MCx.pkl and TCx.pkl have a 200 pA series in the files; 7 have exactly the pickle's steps, and the maximum spike counts of 67 of 68 are within 10% of the pickle's (Spearman 0.996). The link holds for the cells in the dataset; 47 cells of the paper's table cannot be linked as they are absent.
deviations: All features are computed here from the traces, as the paper's extraction code was not deposited, with the definitions of STAR Methods and the standard choices named in the claims file and the helper (peak and steady-state windows, linear range of the V-I relation, averaged chirp profiles, fAHP window, spike detection, filtering). Added after verification round 1, a sweep check of the 1 s hyperpolarizing steps (a sweep must hyperpolarize, from a baseline below -40 mV, with the voltage below -20 mV in the step; 13 sweeps of 10 cells rejected) and a chirp check (a profile with no 3 dB cutoff after its maximum is left out; 1 cell), standard choices of this attempt.

Files hold several runs of each protocol; the paper does not say which it used. The first run is used (for the 1 s steps, the first series reaching 1 nA), a standard choice of this attempt; the link check finds the features close to the paper's table (median Spearman 0.957).
The criterion of this link claim was written by the author after the first comparison of features with the table had been seen during development.

findings.statement: The files carry no cortical area, brain region, slice preparation (acute or culture), transcriptomic or predicted subclass, retrograde label or drug condition, and session_description is a placeholder. These come only from the per-cell tables of the paper's code on Zenodo, matched by the electrode cell_id, which every file has. For the 51 L5 ET cells the table lists with synaptic blockers, only one file records when they were applied (cell QN23.26.013.4A.05.01, user comment "started washon of synaptic block" at sweep 91, after 13 of its 10 s sweeps); no other user comment, sweep comment or lab notebook text mentions a blocker or a wash, so for the other 50 cells when blockers were applied cannot be read from the files.

47 of the 341 cells of the code's L5 physiology table (35 of them recorded by one user) are not in the dandiset, which holds 294; the paper reports 333 cells in its physiology analysis, 33 of them from earlier studies.

File sub-Q19-26-009 (cell Q19.26.009.2A.04.02) names subject Q19.26.009 where the paper's table gives donor Q19.26.012, and the two files of subject Q19.01.001 give Macaca mulatta (NCBITaxon 9544) where the table gives M. nemestrina.

One subject has sex U and subject Q19.01.001 has age P1Y/ (1 year, in a malformed ISO duration), where the paper reports animals of 2 to 19 years; the files hold 57 subjects, 22 male, 34 female, against the paper's 58, 23 and 35.

Five files hold 1 s current command steps above 4 nA (up to 16 nA) in their 200 pA series, beyond the 4 nA that STAR Methods give as the headstage limit; whether these currents were delivered is not stated.

Files hold several runs of each protocol (repeats, series stopped early, a 50 pA and a 200 pA series, runs before and after drug application) and nothing marks which sweeps the paper's features use. For 61 of the 68 cells of the 4 nA analysis the steps in the files differ from those of the code's pickles.

Question for the authors. Were the random training splits of the logistic regression classifiers (Figure 3E to 3G and 5E) stratified by class, and with what regularization? predict_subclass was not deposited. Here the weighted f1 holding out 50% is 78.3% (stratified) or 77.5% (unstratified), against 87.9%.

Question for the authors. How were the subthreshold oscillations of Figure 7 and S7 computed (the curve fitted to find the return to baseline after the AHP, the filter, the smoothing of the spline, the measure of strength, and which sweeps enter Figure S7G)? The R code was not deposited. Rebuilt from the Methods with a smoothing spline over each sweep's segment spectra, the MCx frequency rises with membrane potential as reported, but the spline maximum lies at the 3 Hz edge of the band in 52% of sweeps, oscillation strength does not rise with membrane potential, and the TCx autocorrelation frequency falls with membrane potential.

Question for the authors. Which sweeps of each protocol were used for the features, and how were threshold and half-width of late spikes in the 4 nA trains measured? The extraction code was not deposited; the per-step outputs in MCx.pkl carry the names of the Allen Institute's IPFX. The last-to-first half-width ratio in TCx is 1.55 with the Methods' definition and 2.84 with IPFX's width here, against 2.27 in the code's pickle.
The paper's table holds SFA as the last ISI over the second, the inverse of the STAR Methods' ratio of the second ISI to the last (Spearman -0.989 with the Methods' ratio computed here).

The Figure 6D and 6E legend says TCx L5 ET neurons have a deeper fast AHP and more symmetrical spikes than MCx ones; the Results and the code's means say the opposite, and the data here agree with the Results (fAHP -15.9 against -11.4 mV, up/down ratio 2.69 against 3.31, MCx against TCx).
The paper's deposited morphology features (RawFeatureWide.csv) cover 19 reconstructions, 10 MCx and 9 TCx, where the paper reports 12 and 11.

In 10 files the first run of 1 s hyperpolarizing steps holds sweeps that do not hyperpolarize the cell, start from a baseline above -40 mV or reach -20 mV (13 sweeps; some read 0 mV, as from a lost recording), and nothing in the files marks them. Used as they are, they gave negative steady-state input resistances for 3 cells.

entries.title: Morpho-electric specializations of macaque L5 ET neurons (Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. 2024)
entries.description: Tests the physiology findings of Dembrow, Sawchuk et al. (2024) on dandiset 001065, which holds the current clamp recordings of 294 deep-layer neurons of macaque motor and temporal cortex. Features are computed from the traces; area, preparation and subclass labels come from the paper's per-cell tables on Zenodo. It compares L5 ET with other neurons, L5 ET neurons of the two areas, firing to 4 nA, irregular firing and subthreshold oscillations, and tests the dendritic findings on the paper's deposited morphology features.
